mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a significant labor market contraction, leading to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a rise in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a demand-side shock with inflationary pressure, leading to reduced real consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 10% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and CPIAUCSL changes on negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to increased investment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
